newsitem.title: USA: BankBoston launches urban development unit.
newsitem.headline: BankBoston launches urban development unit.

text.p: BankBoston Corp on Wednesday formally launched an urban development unit to invest an estimated $100 million in businesses owned by minorities and women in communities in four New England states and Florida.

"BankBoston Development Co is the first investment bank for the urban community in America," U.S. Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig said at a press conference in Boston. "This is a very significant development."

The bank was set up at the urging of the office of comptroller, who is the chief federal banking regulator, and amid demands by urban community leaders for banks to take a greater role in financing devolpment in their neighborhoods, BankBoston Development President Grady Hedgespeth said.

BankBoston Development will invest as much as $1.5 million directly in urban companies, often owned by minorities or women, with sales of more than $500,000. It will also take a direct stake in affordable housing projects and provide capital for existing small businesses to help them grow.

Its projected $100 million investment in Massachusetts, Connecticut, Rhode Island, New Hampshire and parts of Florida should stimulate $500 million of new financial resources in urban areas, BankBoston said.
The unit's first deal is a $6.5 million investment to rehabilitate a 227-unit affordable housing project in the Boston neighborhood of Roxbury.

Kenneth Guscott, president of the Long Bay Management Co, one of the Boston's largest minority-owned real estate developers, said his company's partnership with BBDC would help create jobs in the area.
"What's needed is a level playing field, and that's what the Bank of Boston provided us," he said.
